title: Balls of different counts: each ball is equally likely
familyTitle: Probability of a colour drawn from a bag
skill: Classical probability of a colour from a bag with unequal colour counts.

knowledge: probability = favourable ÷ total for equally likely outcomes

concept: Each marble (or ball) is equally likely to be picked, not each colour. So count marbles, not colours.
Probability = (marbles that fit) ÷ (ALL the marbles). It is a number from 0 to 1, never more than 1.
explanation.visualNote: anbag has no figure; a colour table (existing table visual) is proposed.

workedExamples.prompt: A bag has 6 red, 3 blue balls, all of the same size. One ball is taken out without looking. What is the probability that it is blue? Give a fraction.
lines: All the balls: 6 red + 3 blue = 9, each equally likely

hints: Count the balls of the colour asked.
Write the second over the first.

alternativeExplanation.title: Out of
text: The probability is how many balls belong to the colour, out of how many balls there are.

alternativeMethods.name: Number every ball
example: number the balls; each number is equally likely
